slides.title: Factor vs Alpha
bullets:
FOUNDATIONS
Trait → sort → return

FACTOR
A characteristic is an observable trait. Sorting creates factor returns such as HML; a signal ranks stocks. Alpha is the regression intercept left after the chosen model, which also determines whether a return pattern is anomalous.

FOUNDATIONS
Models can absorb yesterday’s anomaly; what survives depends on the benchmark.

slides.title: Anomaly Is Relative
bullets:
DEFINITIONS
An anomaly is benchmark-dependent: specify the model before calling a return pattern unexplained. Tests against broader model sets ask whether the premium survives controls.

Characteristic
An observable firm trait, such as book-to-market.

Factor return
A return series formed by sorting stocks on a characteristic, such as HML.

Signal
A cross-sectional score ranks stocks for portfolio construction.

Unexplained
A pattern the selected benchmark model fails to explain.

Alpha
The regression intercept left unexplained by chosen factors.

Model-relative
Expanded benchmarks can absorb yesterday’s anomaly exposures.

slides.title: CAPM Prices Beta
bullets:
Pricing rule
CAPM makes expected excess return proportional to market beta times the market risk premium; its Security Market Line is linear under the model assumptions.

Beta
Beta is covariance with the market divided by market-return variance; only systematic risk is priced. Two-fund separation gives all investors the same risky mix; market clearing makes it the market portfolio.

Equilibrium
w_mkt ∝ Σ⁻¹(μ − r_f1); μ − r_f1 ∝ Σw_mkt.

slides.title: CAPM Limits
bullets:
CAPM
Flat SML

CAPM
The empirical SML was flatter than CAPM predicts; BAB formalizes the low-beta pattern. Size and value returns exceeded beta-only predictions. These failures did not kill factor-based asset pricing; research shifted to multifactor models.

ROLL (1977)
The true market spans unobservable bonds, real estate and human capital; equity-only CAPM tests are limited. This shifted research toward multifactor models.

slides.title: Model Lineage
bullets:
MODEL LINEAGE
Models broaden the benchmark from market risk to characteristic-based returns, investment, profitability and mispricing. Each extension absorbs patterns, but fit depends on factor construction, assumptions and model selection.

CAPM
CAPM links expected excess returns to market beta under a mean-variance efficient market portfolio and homogeneous expectations.

APT
APT assumes a linear factor structure and no-arbitrage, without specifying the factors’ economic identities.

FF3
Adds size (SMB) and value (HML) to market beta after CAPM leaves those return patterns unexplained.

Carhart
Adds a winner-minus-loser momentum return because momentum-sorted portfolios retain alpha against FF3.

FF5 / q
FF5 adds profitability and investment; q uses investment-to-assets and return on equity.

SY / q5
Mispricing clusters and expected growth broaden fit; selection still matters.

bullets:
FAMA–FRENCH 3
Annual 2×3

SORT
Each June, split size at the NYSE median and book-to-market at the 30th / 70th percentiles. The independent sorts form six value-weighted portfolios; SMB contrasts small with big, while HML contrasts high with low book-to-market.

Independent sorts separate size and value exposures.

bullets:

Monthly rebalanced, value-weighted UMD adds winners-minus-losers to FF3; fund attribution links apparent manager skill to momentum. slides.title: FF5 Adds RMW + CMA
bullets:
PROFITABILITY & INVESTMENT
RMW + CMA

RMW
Robust-minus-weak profitability adds operating profitability to the market, size and value factors; it captures differences in firms’ operating strength.

CMA
Conservative-minus-aggressive investment adds an investment dimension, motivated by dividend-discount logic and firms’ investment behavior.

HML
HML can be partly redundant in some samples; its marginal role depends on the test assets and remains debated.

PROFITABILITY & INVESTMENT
Dividend-discount rationale; sample-dependent HML FF5 adds profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA). Broader fit is not a universal verdict; HML may be partly redundant in some samples.

bullets:

Production

Q-FACTOR MODELS
The q model uses market, investment-to-assets (I / A) and return on equity (ROE), linking expected returns to investment and profitability. q5 adds expected growth (EG); independent size, investment and profitability sorts form 27 portfolios.

slides.title: MGMT + PERF
bullets:
MGMT
MGMT clusters investment and accrual anomalies into a composite mispricing factor; its design summarizes related characteristics rather than treating each signal as independent.

PERF
PERF groups profitability and momentum patterns. Together, MGMT and PERF summarize 11 known anomaly characteristics in the Stambaugh–Yuan framework.

Post-hoc caveat
Its horse-race advantage needs caution because construction is post hoc.

slides.title: Testing Models
bullets:
MODEL TESTING
Different tests answer different pricing questions; the test assets and covariance estimates shape the verdict. Regression fit alone does not settle the economic explanation.

Time series
Regress portfolio returns on factor returns; inspect the intercept.

Cross section
Ask whether betas or traits explain average-return differences.

GRS
Jointly test whether test-portfolio alphas equal zero.

Test assets
Changing the portfolios can change the model comparison.

Covariance
GRS depends on estimated residual covariance across portfolios.

Inference
No single regression settles the economic explanation.

slides.title: Premia Stories
bullets:
WHY PREMIA EXIST
Risk compensation, behavioral mispricing and limits to arbitrage compete; a factor may mix them. Risk pays for bad-state exposure. Behavioral errors include overreaction, underreaction and extrapolation. Trading frictions delay correction, while value, momentum, low-volatility and size each have failure stories.

RISK
BAD-STATE LOSSES Pays for losses in adverse states.

BEHV
Overreaction, underreaction and extrapolation move prices.

FRIC
SHORTING LIMITS Shorting limits slow correction.

WHY PREMIA EXIST
Competing stories can overlap

slides.title: Multiple Testing
bullets:
FACTOR ZOO
Trials raise false-discovery risk

ALIASES
Several labels may reflect one latent exposure rather than distinct sources of return; correlated definitions can repackage a signal.

ABSORBED
A broader benchmark can explain an anomaly that appeared under CAPM or FF3, changing the residual claim.

SELECTION
Many trials make a t-stat above 2 weak evidence; require a rationale, point-in-time data, robustness and independent confirmation.

FACTOR ZOO
Net costs can erase a premium Trading costs may erase the premium. Test incremental value against known factors, model realistic implementation and record the full search process.

bullets:
FACTOR SCORECARD
No factor story is a verdict; each one needs a failure test.

TEST

slides.title: Factor Families
bullets:
TAXONOMY
Each factor family needs controls suited to its signal, data source and likely confounds. Families can overlap, but their measurement risks differ.

Value
B / P, E / P and EBIT / EV; control industry, profitability and leverage.

Momentum
12–1, residual and earnings signals; test reversal and crash exposure.

Quality
GP / A, ROE and accruals; control sector, leverage and size.

Investment
Asset growth, capex growth and net issuance; check profitability.

Risk / liq.
Beta, volatility and spreads / turnover; control sector, leverage, size and price.

Sentiment / alt.
Revisions, short interest, news and web data require coverage and timestamp controls.

slides.title: The 2×3 Sort
bullets:
2×3 SORT
Independent sorts

SIZE
Split the universe into small and big by market capitalization; independently sort the chosen characteristic into low, middle and high buckets.

INTERSECT
Cross the two rankings to form six portfolios; compare high with low within each size group.

HML
HML averages the high-characteristic portfolios and subtracts the low-characteristic average across size buckets.

2×3 SORT
HML = ½(SmallHigh + BigHigh) − ½(SmallLow + BigLow). Higher characteristic returns minus lower, averaged across size.；A Fama-French-style 2×3 sort works as follows: split the universe into small / big by market cap, split the characteristic into low / mid / high by breakpoints, then form six portfolios. Independent sorting keeps the characteristic spread from merely proxying for firm size; the same template applies to profitability or investment.
